4th Period.workingNow: Sorting real tools into 'AI or not AI?' and writing down 3 examples of AI you already use.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A persuasive 'How I Think We Should Use AI' article live on your portfolio site — your argued position on the best way to use AI, backed by this week's research, plus at least one image — pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can define artificial intelligence and identify examples of it so that I can tell the difference between AI and regular software.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.IC.1 — Compare tradeoffs associated with computing technologies that affect people's everyday activities and career options.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: I do: define AI, rule-based vs. learned (10 min)
We do: sort tools into AI or not AI as a class (10 min)
You do: notes — 3 examples of AI you already use (20 min)
Exit Ticket: In your own words, what is AI? (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Your Snake game is finished — nice work. Before you can argue anything about AI, you need an accurate idea of what it actually is, so today we define it and sort real tools into AI and not-AI. Tomorrow we look at what happens to the words you type into one, and by the end of the week your own argued opinion is published on your site.

6th Period.workingNow: Listing the mechanics — the rules, objects, and actions — of a game you already know well.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: MDA framework notes (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) + a one-page Game Design Plan for your SchoolAI game, shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can name the mechanics of a game so that I can start designing the rules and pieces of my own game.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Design and iteratively develop computational artifacts for practical intent, personal expression, or to address a societal issue.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: I do: naming mechanics in a familiar game (10 min)
We do: list a shared game's mechanics together (10 min)
You do: brainstorm mechanics for your own game idea (20 min)
Exit Ticket: List 3 mechanics for your game (5 min)
6th Period.connections: You just finished your Grow Box — a program that reacts to the player. Today we zoom out to the pieces every game is built from: its mechanics, the rules and objects a player actually uses. Hang onto this paper — tomorrow you pick the feeling you want those rules to create.
